summary:
Yana Zhdanova is a Ukrainian feminist activist and leading member of FEMEN, the protest movement known for topless demonstrations. After joining the group in 2008, she took part in actions against prostitution, domestic violence, abortion restrictions and authoritarian governments. Ukrainian police arrested her several times; after a raid on FEMEN’s Kyiv office in August 2013, she left for France and received political asylum in February 2014.

In 2014, Zhdanova damaged a wax statue of Vladimir Putin at Paris’s Grévin Museum and was convicted of destruction and sexual exhibition. France’s Court of Cassation later ruled that, although exposing breasts in public can constitute sexual exhibition, convicting her in this case would disproportionately interfere with her freedom of expression because the act was political. The decision became known as the “Zhdanova jurisprudence” and was cited in 2021 when prosecutors declined to pursue a French actress who had disrobed in a political protest.

Zhdanova and Sasha Shevchenko co-founded the FEMEN association in France in 2016.
